question: Universal Containers (UC) operates worldwide, with offices in more than 100 regions in 10 different countries, and has established a very complex Role Hierarchy to control data visibility. In the new fiscal year, UC is planning to reorganize the roles and reassign account owners. Which feature should an architect recommend to avoid problems with this operation?
optionA: Partition data using Divisions
optionB: Skinny table
optionC: Deferred Sharing Recalculation
explanation:
Reorganizing roles and reassigning many account owners triggers a massive sharing recalculation that can degrade performance and cause lock errors. Deferred Sharing Recalculation lets the admin suspend automatic group-membership and sharing-rule processing during the bulk change and process it afterward. Divisions only partition data for queries and skinny tables are a read-performance structure, so neither addresses the recalculation load.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.security_sharing_defer_sharing_calculations.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.draes.meta/draes/draes_tools_deferred_sharing_maintenance.htm

question: Universal Containers (UC) delivers training and courses to students and companies. UC is implementing a Salesforce Customer Community for its students granting them a Customer Community license. As part of the community requirements, UC asked to give students access to cases that are related to their account in the UC community. What is the optimum sharing technique to achieve these requirements?
optionA: Use Apex sharing to share cases with the students.
optionB: Create a sharing rule to share cases with the students.
optionC: Create a sharing set to share cases with the students.
explanation:
Customer Community licenses have no roles, so role-hierarchy and sharing-rule approaches do not apply and Apex is unnecessary overhead. A Sharing Set is the purpose-built, declarative mechanism that grants community users access to records associated with their own Account or Contact via the lookup, exactly matching cases-by-account. Apex sharing (A) could work but is far more maintenance than the Sharing Set designed for this case.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.networks_setting_light_users.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.users_license_types_communities.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers is implementing Sales Cloud. During the final quarter of the financial year, sales managers help each other close deals. They requested a solution in Salesforce to allow them to share opportunities with other sales managers from different teams as needed. They also requested that sharing deals should expire automatically 2 weeks after the new fiscal year starts. Which proposed solution meets the requirements?
optionA: Apex sharing to share opportunities with sales managers
optionB: Scheduled Apex job to remove access
optionC: Sharing rules to share opportunities with sales managers
explanation:
Ad-hoc, as-needed sharing among managers from different teams has no fixed role or criteria pattern, so it requires programmatic Apex managed sharing to grant access on demand. A scheduled Apex job then deletes those share rows two weeks into the new fiscal year to satisfy the auto-expiry requirement. Sharing rules (C) are owner- or criteria-based and can neither target arbitrary peers nor expire automatically.
References:
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_bulk_sharing_understanding.htm
https://architect.salesforce.com/fundamentals/platform-sharing-architecture

question: At Universal Containers, there's a team of auditors distributed throughout the organization that all need access to high-value opportunities. With a Private sharing model, which option should an architect recommend when designing a solution for this requirement?
optionA: Create a criteria-based sharing rule to grant a public group access to high-value opportunities.
optionB: Add the auditors to the default Opportunity Team.
optionC: Put the auditors at the highest level of the Role Hierarchy.
explanation:
With a Private model, a criteria-based sharing rule keyed on the high-value flag grants the auditors (collected in a public group) access regardless of where they sit in the org. Adding them to the Opportunity Team (B) is manual, per-record, and unscalable for a distributed audit team. Placing them atop the Role Hierarchy (C) would expose all opportunities, not just the high-value ones.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.security_sharing_rules_criteria.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.user_groups.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers (UC) uses a custom Lightning component with an Apex class to display shipment information (custom object, Private organization-wide default). UC sales managers are complaining about two important points: Shipment records that belong to their teams can be seen by other users. Shipment amount should be visible only by managers, but sales reps are able to view it. Which feature did the development team miss that is causing the problems?
optionA: Use isShareable keyword in Apex classes to assure record visibility.
optionB: Use isAccessible() method in Apex classes to check field accessibility.
optionC: Use runAs in test class to enforce user permissions and field level permissions.
explanation:
Of the three options, only isAccessible() names a real mechanism. Enforce Object and Field Permissions documents Schema.DescribeFieldResult.isAccessible() as the check for a field's read access, so calling it before returning the shipment amount is what keeps that field away from sales reps. "isShareable" is not an Apex construct, and runAs is a testing method, not a runtime safeguard.
Be careful about the first complaint in the stem, though: isAccessible() does nothing about it. Records visible to the wrong users is a record-access problem, fixed by the class's sharing declaration (or by running the query in user mode), not by a field describe. No option offered here addresses it.
One version note worth carrying: how much Apex enforces by default has moved. In API version 66.0 and earlier Apex runs in system mode by default; in 67.0 and later it runs in user mode, so the running user's permissions and field-level security are enforced unless the code opts into system mode. An @AuraEnabled class that declares no sharing keyword has long used an implicit "with sharing".
References:
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_classes_perms_enforcing.htm
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_security_sharing_rules.htm
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/apex-security.html

Nothing in the option set fixes the record-visibility complaint, which needs a sharing declaration or a user-mode query — so the item is defective as printed.

question: Universal Containers (UC) is in a legal dispute regarding several orders. UC has found out these records were removed from the system. The VP of Sales has asked to ensure this cannot happen in the future. Which approach should meet this requirement?
optionA: Change the Record Type/Page Layout assignment for Orders to be Read-Only.
optionB: Remove the Delete button from the Order Page Layout.
optionC: Remove Order Delete permission from profiles and permission sets.
explanation:
Deleting records is governed by object-level CRUD on profiles and permission sets, so removing the Delete permission is the only reliable way to prevent deletion through any channel, including the API and Apex. Removing the Delete button from a layout (B) merely hides it in the UI and does not stop list-view or API deletes. Record-type or layout changes (A) do not control delete at all.

https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.managing_the_sharing_model.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A junior account manager owns an account and creates a new opportunity to manage a complex deal. She needs the help of the product specialist and solution engineer. Given the size of this deal, she knows the account is likely to be reassigned to a senior account manager in the near future. What is the optimal way for the junior account manager to share the opportunity, given the private sharing model?
optionA: Manual share on the opportunity
optionB: Manual share on the account
optionC: Opportunity Team
explanation:
An opportunity team is the durable way to bring the product specialist and solution engineer onto this deal. The two mechanisms differ precisely on what happens at a transfer: "User managed sharing is removed when the record owner changes", and Salesforce walks through the same behaviour under the hood — "When a record owner changes, Salesforce deletes its associated sharing rows with Manual row causes." Team-based access is not a manual share and is not swept away with them.
That matters here because the junior account manager expects the deal to move. Once the opportunity is reassigned, a manual share on it is gone and the specialists silently lose access; the team survives the handover.
Sharing the account instead grants nothing on the opportunity — access flows implicitly from child up to parent, not from parent down to child.

question: A sales coach at Universal Containers wants to create and share a report folder with other sales coaches. Which two permissions are required to accomplish this?
optionA: Create Report Folders and manage Reports in Public Folders
optionB: Create and customize Reports and Report Folders
optionC: Manage Reports in Public Folders and edit My Reports
explanation:
Creating a report folder requires the "Create Report Folders" permission, and sharing or managing what is inside a public report folder requires "Manage Reports in Public Folders"; together they let the coach build and share the folder (option A). Option B covers building reports and customizing them, not the folder-sharing administration this scenario needs. This corrects the source, which selected the report-building option rather than the folder-management pair.

question: Universal Containers uses 75,000 distributors that have close to 1 million total users. Distributors need opportunities assigned to the distributor for delivery. What license recommendation will meet distributor needs?
optionA: Sales Cloud
optionB: Customer Community Plus
optionC: Partner Community
optionD: Customer Community
explanation:
Distributors that need opportunities assigned to them for delivery are channel partners performing sales and CRM work, which requires Partner Community because it supports Opportunities and partner roles. Customer Community and Customer Community Plus are oriented to support and self-service, and Customer Community lacks roles and full CRM objects. The one-million-user volume is supported under Partner Community licensing.

question: Universal Containers would like to control access to records and objects according to the following business requirements: Sales users can view all account records but only edit their own records. Sales managers can view all account records but only edit records of their team. Service users can view all account records that are not marked with a RecordType of Prospect. Which organization-wide default configuration should an architect recommend to fulfill these requirements?
optionA: Public Read Write
optionB: Public Read/Transfer
optionC: Private
explanation:
Only a Private OWD lets you start from no access and layer the differentiated rules: edit-own for sales users, edit-team for managers via role hierarchy, and record-type-based exclusions for service users. Public Read/Write (A) or Read/Transfer (B) would grant visibility and edit too broadly and could not enforce "edit only your own or your team's" records. A restrictive baseline is the prerequisite for all the layered grants.

https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.security_sharing_owd_about.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.managing_the_sharing_model.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers (UC) has a team that analyzes customer orders looking for fraud. This team needs access to Invoice records (custom object, Private organization-wide default). UC has complex rules to control users' access. The architect recommended using Apex managed sharing to meet these requirements. Which recommendation should a developer consider when implementing the changes?
optionA: Use "Without Sharing" keyword to make sure record visibility will be considered.
optionB: Use "With Sharing" keyword to enforce Field-Level Security.
optionC: Use runAs system method to test different users accessing these records.
explanation:
Apex managed sharing inserts share rows in system context, so the safeguard against improper access is rigorous testing; runAs() in test methods validates that each user sees only the records intended. The "Without Sharing" keyword (A) would ignore the user's access and worsen the risk, and "With Sharing" does not enforce Field-Level Security, so option B's stated rationale is incorrect.
References:
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_security_sharing_rules.htm
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_testing_tools_runas.htm

question: Which functionality does the system method "runAs()" verify when writing test methods?
optionA: Enforcement of a user's record sharing
optionB: Enforcement of a user's Field-Level Security
optionC: Enforcement of a user's permissions
explanation:
Record sharing is the answer this item wants, and it is the answer the exam keys. Read the current documentation carefully, though, because the item is broken against it: Using the runAs Method says that after the user context switches, "the user's sharing rules and object-level and field-level permissions are enforced", and repeats it — "The user's sharing rules and object-level and field-level permissions are enforced within a runAs block, regardless of the sharing mode (with sharing or without sharing) of the test class."
So all three options describe something runAs enforces today. The reason A is still the best answer is that record sharing is the thing runAs exists for: outside a runAs block Apex generally runs in system mode, where object- and field-level permissions of the running user are not taken into account, and runAs is the only way a test can put itself in a specific user's record-access shoes.
If you need to assert object or field permissions in code rather than in a test, that is a separate mechanism — user-mode database operations, or the Schema describe methods isAccessible, isCreateable and isUpdateable.
References:
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_testing_tools_runas.htm
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_classes_perms_enforcing.htm

corrected.note: Answer stands, but the old explanation stated that runAs "does not enforce the user's object permissions or Field-Level Security" and that "under runAs, Apex still executes in system mode for CRUD and FLS". The Apex Developer Guide says the opposite: object-level and field-level permissions are enforced inside a runAs block. Treat the item as defective — all three options are true of runAs as currently documented.

question: A consulting company uses the Salesforce mobile app for its field consultants and uses Case object to track customer specific consulting done by field consultants. The company also has a large number of customer service representatives who takes calls from customers on company issued desktops and uses case object to track customer issues and grievances. The company would like to capture images of customer site captured by field consultants while they are editing the case record during customer site visit. The Director of IT wants to minimize customization and promote reuseability of code artifacts wherever possible. What recommendations should an architect give to the company to implement the image capture requirement, while ensuring customer that the service rep can continue to use same lightning pages they were trained to use?
optionA: Use Lightning Component as an override for "Edit" action on mobile view allowing image capture feature. No Change required for desktop users.
optionB: Use Lightning Component as an override for "Edit" action on lightning experience allowing image capture feature. Detect the form factor of the device and redirect the user to the default not overridden view.
optionC: Create a separate button "Edit in Mobile", which opens a custom lightning component that will allow field consultants to add an image. No change required for desktop users.
explanation:
Overriding the Edit action only on the mobile view adds image capture for field consultants while leaving desktop service reps on the standard Lightning pages they were trained on, maximizing reuse and minimizing customization. Option B introduces form-factor detection and redirect complexity, and a separate custom button (C) is extra customization the Director explicitly wanted to avoid.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.assign_action_overrides.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.standard_actions_overrides.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers requested to leverage Lightning Web Components (LWC) to improve support reps' user experience. LWC will be used as view layer, and Apex classes will have the business logic. Which attention points should the development team consider when implementing this solution?
optionA: Once that Apex runs on system mode, the development team needs to enforce record visibility.
optionB: Create test classes including runAs to test different users accessing the data.
optionC: Use isShareable, isEditable, and isCreatable to enforce field permissions.
explanation:
Option A is the only choice that names a genuine security consideration, and it is the exam key. Option C is disqualified outright — "isShareable" does not exist; the Schema describe methods are isAccessible, isCreateable and isUpdateable. Option B is good practice but describes a test, not an implementation concern.
The premise inside A has aged, so hold it precisely rather than as a slogan. Secure Apex Classes states that "In API version 66.0 and earlier, Apex runs in system mode by default", and that "In API version 67.0 and later, Apex runs in user mode by default, meaning that the current user's permissions and field-level security (FLS) are enforced during code execution." The same page adds that an @AuraEnabled class which sets neither with sharing nor without sharing "uses a default or implicit value of with sharing".
The durable lesson survives the version change: an LWC that reaches data through Apex does not inherit the UI's security for free, so declare the sharing keyword and the access mode explicitly on every class and query rather than relying on whichever default your API version happens to give you.
References:
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/apex-security.html
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_classes_enforce_usermode.htm
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_classes_perms_enforcing.htm
_cat: Permissions to Standard Objects, Custom Objects, and Fields

question: If a Case requires involvement from one of the Legal team, the Case owner adds one of the corporate lawyers to the Legal SME field on the case. Since cases are private, how can we grant a lawyer access to a specific case when their assistance is needed?
optionA: Create a Criteria-Based Sharing Rule that shares to the Corporate Legal Team Role when the "legal assistance needed?" field is checked.
optionB: Use Apex Managed sharing in a case Trigger that shares the record to the user identified in the Legal SME field.
optionC: Create a Criteria Based Sharing Rule that shares to the Legal Public Group when the "legal assistance needed?" field is checked.
explanation:
The lawyer is identified per record in the Legal SME user lookup, so the share target is dynamic and only Apex managed sharing in a Case trigger can share to whichever user populates that field. Criteria-based rules (A and C) can share only to a fixed role or public group, not to an arbitrary user named on each individual case.
References:
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_bulk_sharing_understanding.htm
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.security_sharing_rules_criteria.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers (UC) delivers training in 500 different regions. The UC operations users team manages course setup, scheduling, and trainer setup. The team members work at a regional level and report to an operations manager. The operations manager requested access to edit ALL scheduled courses owned by the operation users team. How should this be achieved?
optionA: The operations manager will get access to the scheduled courses by creating an ownership-based sharing rule and share the scheduled courses with the operations manager.
optionB: The operations manager will get access to the scheduled courses owned by the operations users team defined in the Role Hierarchy.
optionC: The operations manager will get access to the scheduled courses by creating a public group, and add the operations manager and the operations users team to the public group.
explanation:
The operations manager sits above the regional operations users in the Role Hierarchy, and the object grants access up the hierarchy by default, so the manager automatically gets edit access to all scheduled courses the team owns. An ownership-based sharing rule (A) is unnecessary overhead, and a public group (C) does not by itself confer the ownership-based access being requested.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.security_controlling_access_using_hierarchies.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers uses Person Accounts to represent retail customers and Business Accounts to represent commercial customers. The retail sales team should not have access to commercial customers but should have access to ALL retail customers. With the organization-wide default on Account set to Private, how should the architect meet these requirements?
optionA: Create a criteria-based sharing rule giving the Retail Sales role access to Accounts of type Person Account.
optionB: Create an owner-based sharing rule on AccountContactRelation to grant access to all account contact roles records owned by retail sales reps.
optionC: Update the Retail Sales profile to grant access to Person Account record type.
explanation:
With Account set to Private, a criteria-based sharing rule matching the Person Account record type grants the Retail Sales role access to all retail customers while leaving Business (commercial) accounts hidden. Profile record-type access (C) governs creation and layout assignment, not record visibility, and an AccountContactRelation rule (B) does not grant the needed account access.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.security_sharing_rules_criteria.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.security_sharing_owd_about.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers (UC) has a partner community for its 200 distributors. UC customer accounts are assigned an individual distributor. The organization-wide default setting for the custom Delivery object is Private. How should an architect advise UC to grant all users at a distributor access to delivery records for all customers assigned to a particular distributor?
optionA: Create a criteria based sharing rule that shares delivery records matching a distributor to the Distributor role in the Role Hierarchy.
optionB: Create a criteria-based sharing rule that shares delivery records matching the Distributor to users of a Public Group created for the distributor.
optionC: Create a Sharing Set for the Distributor profile to grant access to the Delivery object.
explanation:
A sharing set is the scalable answer for site users, and it is configured per profile — "You can have one sharing set per profile only" — so a single Delivery mapping covers every user at every distributor instead of 200 per-distributor rules.
Sharing rules are the wrong tool at this scale. Partner users do have roles, but each partner account gets its own three-role hierarchy, so there is no single "Distributor role" to target, and a rule per distributor does not scale to 200.
One caveat on the mapping. A sharing set grants access to records "associated with an account or contact that matches the user's account or contact", and access mappings support indirect lookups. Whether one mapping can reach Delivery records that hang off the customer account rather than the distributor account depends on how the Delivery-to-account relationship is modelled; if the lookup chain does not resolve to the user's own account, the sharing set has to be designed around that. Treat C as the right family of solution rather than a configuration you can copy unexamined.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.networks_setting_light_users.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.networks_partner_roles_overview.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers' organization wide-defaults model is Private for the Account object. A sales rep owns two opportunities in one Account. The Sales Rep profile has Create/Edit access to opportunity records. Which level of access will the sales rep have to the related Account record?
optionA: Read access
optionB: Read/Create/Edit access
optionC: No access
explanation:
With the Account OWD Private, owning a child opportunity grants implicit Read-only access to the parent account so the related record is viewable. Implicit parent sharing never grants edit or create on the parent, so Read/Create/Edit (B) and No access (C) are incorrect.
References:
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.draes.meta/draes/draes_object_relationships_implicit_sharing.htm

question: Universal Containers (UC) has created a custom Invoice object. Standard sales users at UC can see the records in search layout, but when they click to view the detail, only record name, created date, and last modified date are shown. When the system admin accesses it, he or she sees the full record detail with many more data fields. What is the likely cause of this issue?
optionA: A role-based sharing rule is missing and should be added for the sales user's role to grant access to the fields.
optionB: The Sales Users profile does not have access to the remaining fields.
optionC: The page layout assigned to Sales User profile has only Read-Only access to the fields.
explanation:
The user can open the record but sees only a few system fields while the admin sees everything, which is the signature of missing Field-Level Security on the Sales Users profile. A sharing rule (A) controls record access, not field visibility, and a read-only page layout (C) would still display the fields rather than hide them. FLS is what determines which fields a profile can read.

https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.checking_field_accessibility_for_a_particular_field.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers (UC) wants to reduce the amount of redundant leads entered into the system. UC also only edited/reassigned by the lead owner. What organization-wide default (OWD) approach should be recommended to help UC implement these requirements?
optionA: Implement a Public Read Only OWD on Lead.
optionB: Implement a Public Read Only/Transfer OWD on Lead
optionC: Implement a private OWD on Lead.
optionD: Implement a Public Read/Write OWD on Lead.
explanation:
Public Read Only is the setting that satisfies both halves of the requirement. Reps can see every existing lead, which is what stops them entering a duplicate, while edit and reassignment stay with the owner and with users above the owner in the role hierarchy.
A Private model would hide leads from everyone but their owner and defeat the deduplication goal outright. Public Read/Write hands editing to the whole org, and the transfer variants add reassignment rights the requirement explicitly reserves for the owner. (Note that "Public Read Only/Transfer" is not a real Lead setting; the transfer option Salesforce offers is Public Read/Write/Transfer.)
References:

https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.managing_the_sharing_model.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers would like to store an encryption key within Salesforce for use in Apex Code, but does not want users to be able to see this confidential key. Users require the view setup permission. How can Universal Containers securely store the confidential key?
optionA: Create a protected custom metadata type that stores the encryption key. Package the protected custom metadata type with its associated records in a managed package. Install the package in the production org.
optionB: Create a protected custom metadata type that stores the encryption key. Package the protected custom metadata type with its associated records in an unlocked package. Install the package in the production org.
optionC: Create a custom metadata type that stores the encryption key. Make sure that only the admin profile has access to the custom metadata type so that end users cannot access the encryption key.
explanation:
A protected custom metadata type packaged in a managed package hides its records even from users who hold View Setup, so the encryption key stays invisible while remaining usable in Apex. Plain custom metadata in the subscriber org (C) is viewable through setup, and an unlocked package (B) does not protect the records the same way a managed package does.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.custommetadatatypes_package_access.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers (UC) is a fast-growing company that sells containers globally. It has thousands of dealerships throughout the world where local dealers service containers. UC implemented a new Partner Community for its dealers. Each dealership has a dealer manager who manages the service agents. The community sharing model is private. What is the optimal option to give dealer managers visibility to customer cases only raised by their service agents?
optionA: Use the Role Hierarchy so that the cases raised by service agents will be visible to their relevant dealer managers.
optionB: Create a sharing rule to share cases created by service agents with their dealer manager.
optionC: Create a sharing group to share cases created by service agents with their dealer manager.
explanation:
In a private community model, dealer managers sit above their service agents in the partner Role Hierarchy, so cases owned by the agents roll up to their relevant manager automatically with no extra configuration. A sharing rule (B) is unnecessary, and a "sharing group" (C) is not the correct construct for this hierarchy-based visibility.

question: The finance team at Universal Containers usually does not have access to account and contact records. A finance analyst was temporarily given opportunity access for a big deal to help with tax calculation. However, she can now also access account and contact records. What is causing this issue?
optionA: Account records can be accessed due to implicit sharing from Opportunity.
optionB: Account records can be accessed due to Role Hierarchy.
optionC: Contact records can be accessed due to implicit sharing from Opportunity.
explanation:
Granting access to an opportunity gives implicit Read access to its parent account and related contacts, which is why the finance analyst can suddenly see the account; this is by-design implicit parent sharing from the opportunity. The cause is the opportunity access, not the Role Hierarchy (B), and the question concerns the account specifically.

question: Universal Containers has implemented Customer Community with Customer Community Plus licenses for its distributors. Some distributors requested granting specific community users (agents) to view cases submitted by other agents of the same distributor. Which feature only supports these requirements?
optionA: Permission set to grant community admin permission
optionB: Delegate external user
optionC: Partner super user
explanation:
Customer Community Plus has roles, and the Partner/Customer Super User permission lets a user see records owned by other users of the same account at their role and below, which is exactly "view cases of other agents of the same distributor." A community-admin permission set (A) or delegated external user administration (B) manage users, not record visibility.

question: Who can view a PDF that is uploaded to the Files Home private library by a user?
optionA: The user and users above them in the Role Hierarchy
optionB: The user and users with View All Data permission
optionC: Only the user
explanation:
A file in a private library is visible to its owner and to nobody else. Who Can See My File? makes the point twice over, once for each of the permissions people expect to override it: "Users with Modify All Data permission have built-in access to files that they don't own… However, if the file is in a private library, then only the file owner has access to it", and "Users with View All Data permission can view and preview files that they don't own. However, if the file is in a private library, then only the file owner has access to it."
The role hierarchy does not enter into it at all — file visibility is not derived from role, so option A is wrong for a different reason than option B.
One distinction the stem blurs: a plain upload in Files home is private in the sense that it has not been shared, but the owner plus users with Modify All Data can still find it. Only the private library carves out even those permissions.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?language=en_US&id=sf.collab_files_settings_perms.htm&type=5

question: Besides their own team accounts, sales managers at Universal Containers (UC) need Read access to all accounts of the same segment in other countries. Role Hierarchy was implemented accordingly (based on countries), but a sales manager in the U.S. is complaining that he cannot view account records of the same segment in Canada. What should UC do to grant access properly?
optionA: Create an owner-based sharing rule to grant access to account records, that have the same segment, to all sales manager roles.
optionB: Create a public group and include all accounts of the same segment, and then grant access with a permission set.
optionC: Change the Role Hierarchy and put all the sales managers in the U.S. and Canada in the same role.
explanation:
A sharing rule that shares same-segment accounts to every sales-manager role gives the U.S. manager visibility into Canadian same-segment accounts that the country-based Role Hierarchy cannot provide laterally. Merging the roles (C) would break the country hierarchy, and a permission set (B) cannot grant record access based on segment. Note the option says "owner-based," though sharing on a segment value is technically criteria-based, so the wording is imprecise.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.security_sharing_rules_criteria.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Dreamforce presenters need to be able to edit their presentation details (summary, presenter biographies, etc) on a private custom object in Salesforce (Presentation). All presenters for a presentation are captured on a Presenters junction object between Presenter and User. How can this be accomplished?
optionA: Give Edit rights to the Presentation record via a Permission set that is given to the Presenters for a record.
optionB: Trigger on Presenter junction object that adds the user to the Sales Team for the Presentation record.
optionC: Trigger on Presenter junction object that uses Apex Managed sharing to add or remove access to the related Presentation record.
explanation:
Presenters are linked through a Presenters junction and need edit access on the related private Presentation, so a trigger that uses Apex managed sharing to add or remove the user's access as junction records change is the precise solution. A permission set (A) grants object-level access rather than record-level, and adding to a Sales Team (B) does not apply to this custom object.

https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_bulk_sharing_understanding.htm

question: Universal Containers (UC) has affiliates who sell containers in countries where UC does not have a local office. UC uses a Partner Community to manage the sales cycle in those countries. One of its affiliates has grown substantially and restructured its internal sales team with the following structure: Sales VP -> Director of Sales -> Sales Manager -> Sales Reps. Sales Reps should not see each others' opportunities, and visibility of deals should open up within a Sales Rep's hierarchy. What is the main problem an architect should address in this situation?
optionA: The Channel Manager role cannot be shared with Partner Community.
optionB: Partner User roles are limited to three Ievels.
optionC: Partner Community does not support Role Hierarchy.
explanation:
Partner Community provides only three partner role levels, so a four-tier reseller hierarchy of VP, Director, Manager, and Rep cannot be modeled directly, which is the core problem an architect must address. Partner Community does support a role hierarchy (so C is false); the limitation is the depth, not the existence, of partner roles.

question: Universal Containers uses the standard Case object to track various support requests sent to servicing agents. Currently, the Case object has more than 400 fields. Eight different types of case processes have been established, each with a unique combination of statuses. The Director of Customer Service wants to ensure that servicing agents see only the required information specific to the case type they are addressing. Which option is recommended to implement this requirement?
optionA: Use Dynamic Forms with different field sections representing the relevant fields per case type, and control visibility of sections by Case Record Type value.
optionB: Use different Page Layouts per case type, each representing the relevant fields per case type.
optionC: Use a custom LWC to override the View action of the Case object, and a Custom Metadata Type to define the relevant fields per case type.
explanation:
Dynamic Forms lets you place fields in sections and show or hide them by Case Record Type on a single Lightning page, meeting the requirement to show only the relevant fields per case type with minimal layouts. Multiple page layouts (B) is the classic alternative and is defensible, but it is heavier to maintain across eight processes and 400 fields. A custom LWC override (C) adds unnecessary code.

question: A custom Invoice object has been created with a master-detail relationship to Account. The accounts receivable (AR) team needs access to invoice records. AR users neither own nor have access to account records. The Account organization-wide default is set to Private. The AR team is unable to find invoices in list views, reports, and Global Search. The architect has been asked to help troubleshoot. What is preventing AR team members from seeing invoices?
optionA: The AR profile does not have Read permission to the Invoice object.
optionB: A sharing rule is missing to share invoices with the AR team.
optionC: A sharing rule is missing to share accounts with the AR team.
explanation:
Because Invoice is master-detail to Account, invoice access is Controlled by Parent, so the AR team cannot see invoices because they cannot see the parent accounts; sharing the Accounts with AR restores visibility everywhere, including list views, reports, and Global Search. The team already has object Read (so A is wrong), and you cannot directly share a detail record (so B is wrong).

question: Universal Containers has expanded to sell virtual containers for data storage. Virtual container work orders are provisioned immediately by the system and therefore cannot be changed by a sales rep. What is an optimal approach to implement these requirements?
optionA: Change the Record Type/Page Layout assignment for Work Orders to Read Only.
optionB: Implement a sharing rule that changes access for all Work Orders to Read.
optionC: Remove the Work Order Edit permission from the Sales Representative profile.
explanation:
Provisioned virtual work orders must be non-editable by reps, and removing the Edit object permission on the Sales Representative profile is the clean, system-wide enforcement. Record-type or layout read-only settings (A) do not block edits made through the API, and a sharing rule (B) controls record access rather than edit capability at the object level.

question: Users at Universal Containers are complaining that a field has disappeared from the Account page after last weekend's deployment. The page layout did not change with this deployment. How should the admin troubleshoot this issue?
optionA: View Field Accessibility in the Object Manager.
optionB: Log in as a user and check several accounts to isolate the problem records.
optionC: Run a Who Sees What report, filtering on Account.
explanation:

question: An architect has a requirement to create a criteria-based sharing rule based on the customer Social Security Number. However, when setting up the rule in Contact Sharing, the field is not shown on the list of available fields. What is causing this issue?
optionA: The architect does not have permission to Compliance fields.
optionB: The field has been configured for encryption.
optionC: The architect's profile does not have Field-Level Security for this field.
explanation:
Classic-encrypted fields cannot be used in criteria-based sharing rule filters, so the encrypted Social Security Number field is absent from the available-fields list, which is the platform restriction at play. Lacking FLS (C) would hide the field on layouts but is not why it is specifically unavailable for sharing-rule criteria.

optionA: Roles
optionB: users
optionC: Profiles

question: Universal Containers (UC) is a non-profit organization with more than 20,000,000 members (donors). UC decided to assign those accounts to donations reps based on their regions. Donations reps ended up owning more than 50,000 donors each. The donation reps started to see significant degradation of the system performance. What is the reason for this problem?
optionA: The donations reps' access to the assigned accounts is wrong.
optionB: Salesforce sharing recalculation kicked off.
optionC: There is an Account ownership data skew problem.
explanation:
Tens of thousands of accounts owned by individual donation reps creates account ownership data skew, which causes sharing and recalculation contention and the observed performance degradation. The access design itself is not wrong (A), and recalculation (B) is a symptom rather than the root cause; the skew is the underlying problem.

optionA: Replace opportunity owner.
optionB: Update opportunity stage.
optionC: Add/remove members in the opportunity team.

question: A sales rep (John) at Universal Containers (UC) requested to update information in an account record where he has READ only access. John requested the EDIT access permission from the owner of the record (Paul). Paul manually shared the record with John. Assuming the OWD of the Account object is Public Read-Only, what is the impact in the system?
optionA: New AccountShare record is created. Row Cause is "Manual" and Access Level is "Read/Write".
optionB: Existing AccountShare record is updated. Row Cause is "Owner" and User/Group is "John".
optionC: New AccountShare record is created. Row Cause is "Owner" and Access Level is "Full".
optionD: Existing AccountShare record is updated. Row Cause is "Manual" and Access Level is "Read/Write".
explanation:
Manually granting Read/Write on a Public Read-Only account creates a new AccountShare row with row cause "Manual" and access level Read/Write. The baseline Read-only access comes from the OWD rather than from an "Owner" share row that gets updated, so the descriptions in B, C, and D mischaracterize the resulting share record.

question: Sales Operations at Universal Containers (UC) has created Public Report and Dashboard folders for sales managers that report to the VP of sales. Sales Operations currently spends a few hours each month updating users that should have access to edit items in these folders. In which two ways can UC grant access to sales managers to automate access to these Reports and Dashboards folders? Choose 2 answers
optionA: Share the folders lowest roles in the role hierarchy, Superiors will get access automatically.
optionB: Share the folders with the "VP of Sales" Role and Subordinates.
optionC: Share the folders with the "Sales Managers" Queue.
optionD: Share the folders with a "Sales Managers" Public Group.
explanation:
Report and dashboard folders can be shared with a role and its subordinates or with a public group, both of which automatically include the right managers and eliminate the monthly manual upkeep. Sharing to the lowest roles expecting superiors to inherit (A) is false because folder access does not roll up the hierarchy, and folders cannot be shared with queues (C).

question: Sales reps at Universal Containers (UC) complain about the manual activities they need to perform in order to grant access to supporting internal users (legal, engineering, finance, etc.) for customer records when they need help. In general, the sales reps involved in the deals will not change. How should an architect help UC improve sales reps' productivity?
optionA: Create a permission set with View All Data and assign to supporting users.
optionB: Create a criteria based sharing rule to grant access to other users.
optionC: Leverage default Account team.
explanation:
Because the same supporting users repeatedly help on the rep's deals, a default Account Team auto-adds them to new accounts, removing the manual sharing while scoping access appropriately. View All Data (A) massively over-grants, and a criteria-based rule (B) does not fit the pattern of specific recurring helpers per rep.

question: An architect from a previous project implemented Platform Shield Encryption for a company. However, based on a recent audit, the company's Privacy Team identified three additional fields in their Account Records (Billing Street, Billing City and Phone) that needs to be secure and protected. How should an architect proceed with this new policy change?
optionA: Use Encryption Policy and contact Salesforce to update the existing records so that their field values are encrypted.
optionB: Use Encryption Policy and wait for an email from Salesforce indicating the field values are encrypted.
optionC: Use Classic Encryption to ensure all fields are protected and contact Salesforce for help with encryption verification.
explanation:
Turning on encryption for Billing Street, Billing City and Phone through the encryption policy protects data written from that point on; values already stored stay in the clear until they are re-saved or run through background encryption. So the policy change is only half the job, and the second half is a synchronisation step.
How that step is triggered has changed since this item was written. Salesforce now supports self-service synchronisation from the Encryption Statistics and Data Sync page in Setup for standard and custom fields, the Attachment Content Body field, and field history and feed tracking — with a limit of once every seven days. For everything outside that list you still contact Salesforce Customer Support. Option A therefore remains correct in substance: an explicit background-encryption pass is required, and Salesforce may still have to run it.
Classic Encryption is a separate and weaker feature that applies only to custom text fields, so it is not a route to protecting standard Account fields.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=xcloud.security_pe_mass_encryption.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: (Variant) Which method should be used to grant an unrelated group of users access to a set of records?
optionA: Role Hierarchy
optionB: Sharing Sets
optionC: Public Groups
explanation:
A public group is what you build when the people who need access do not line up with anything the platform already models. Salesforce describes exactly this use: "Use public groups to streamline sharing records with users in different parts of your company that aren't aligned with a single role." Collect the users in the group, then point a sharing rule at it.
The role hierarchy models reporting lines, so it cannot express an arbitrary set of users, and a sharing set grants site users access to records tied to their own account or contact — a community mechanism, not a way to hand a group of internal users a set of records.

https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.user_groups.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.networks_setting_light_users.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: What advanced tool can Salesforce enable for Large-scale role hierarchy realignments?
optionA: Set external organization-wide default to public read only
optionB: Skinny Table Indexing
optionC: Granular locking
optionD: Partitioning by Divisions
explanation:
Granular locking is the feature that makes large realignments survivable. Without it, the sharing system takes a lock over the whole group-membership table during updates, so unrelated role and group changes queue behind one another and callers see "could not acquire lock" errors. With it, "groups that are in separate hierarchies can be manipulated concurrently", users can be added to territories and public groups at the same time, and "a single long-running process, such as a role delete, blocks only a small subset of operations".
Worth knowing for current orgs: granular locking is now enabled by default, so this is less a switch you ask Salesforce to flip than a behaviour you design your maintenance processes around. Salesforce publishes a table of which group operations may run concurrently.
External org-wide defaults, skinny tables and Divisions address visibility, query performance and data partitioning respectively — none of them touches recalculation locking.
References:
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.draes.meta/draes/draes_group_membership_locking.htm

question: Sales operations at Universal Containers (UC) wants to create list views to filter opportunities for certain geographies. How should UC hide list views that are not relevant to an individual user since there will be more than 50 list views?
optionA: Share the list views with the appropriate public group.
optionB: Share the list views with the appropriate queue.
optionC: Share the list views with the appropriate individual users.
explanation:
List views are made visible to a chosen set of users by sharing them with the appropriate public group, so each geography's reps see only the views relevant to them. List views can be shared with public groups or roles but not with queues (B), and per-user sharing (C) does not scale across more than fifty views.

question: To grant Universal Containers sales managers access to shipment records properly, it was necessary to leverage Apex managed sharing. The IT team is worried about improper access to records. What should an architect recommend to mitigate this risk?
optionA: Use isShareable keyword in Apex classes to assure record visibility will be followed.
optionB: Use isAccessible keyword in Apex classes to assure record visibility will be followed.
optionC: Use runAs system method in test classes to test using different users and profiles.
explanation:
Apex managed sharing runs in system context, so the safeguard against improper access is testing with runAs() across different users and profiles to confirm only the intended visibility. The "isSharesble" and "isAccesible keyword" options (A and B) are not valid record-visibility constructs in Apex.

question: Universal Containers has selected a small and diverse group of users to review Inactive accounts. Given the Private sharing model, a public group was created and made available to this group of users. A sharing rule was created to make inactive Accounts visible to the public group. However, some of these users are reporting they don't see any of the Accounts that were shared with the public group. what is the underlying Issue for these users?
optionA: The users are in profiles that have no access to the Account object.
optionB: The page layout assigned to these users is different than the Account owner.
optionC: The users have a permission set that only allow Accounts in "Active' status.
optionD: The Accounts are owned by users higher in the role hierarchy.
explanation:
Sharing rules extend record access only on top of object-level CRUD, so users whose profiles lack Read on the Account object see nothing regardless of the sharing rule. A differing page layout (B) or a status-limited permission set (C) would not explain a complete absence of the shared accounts. Object access is the prerequisite the affected users are missing.

question: The sales managers at Universal Containers requested their teams to define each user's role on their accounts in order to provide an easy way to establish accountability and collaboration. Sales managers also requested that sales associates should only get the following permissions: 1. Read access to the accounts. 2. Read access to cases related to the accounts. 3. No access to deals related to the accounts. The sales associates may be granted access to opportunities when needed. Assuming the overall sharing model of the organization is Private and no sharing rules are configured on the Account object, how should an architect achieve these requirements?
optionA: Use Account teams to define access to accounts as well as opportunities and cases related to accounts.
optionB: Use Account teams and Case teams. No configuration required for the Opportunity object.
optionC: Use Account teams and sharing rules to share cases with sales associates. No change required to the Opportunity object.
explanation:
A single Account Team can grant the defined per-user access, namely Read on accounts and related cases and no opportunity access unless explicitly granted, covering all three requirements through one mechanism. Splitting into Case teams and sharing rules (B and C) is unnecessary because Account Team access settings already control related case and opportunity access.

question: Customer complaints for bad interactions with a customer support agent are logged as Cases and assigned to a human resources representative. The agent of the complaint should not see the case, but their manager should. How is this accomplished?
optionA: Trigger on Case to lookup and share to the manager of an Assigned Agent custom field (the subject of the complaint) using Apex Managed Sharing.
optionB: Criteria based Sharing Rule on Case that shares to the Role Manager and above when a custom field Assigned Agent (subject of the complaint) Is not blank,
optionC: Case is owned by the subject of the complaint, so their manager in the role hierarchy can access the record. CRED permission are removed on Case so the agent cannot read the case record.
explanation:
The complaint must be hidden from the agent but visible to their manager, identified through a custom Assigned Agent field, so a trigger that looks up that agent's manager and shares via Apex managed sharing is the precise solution. A criteria-based rule to "Role Manager and above" (B) over-shares up the chain, and owning the case by the subject (C) would let the agent see it.

question: Universal Containers has created a Reimbursement Custom Object to capture requests for reimbursement of expenses related to office supplies. The Reimbursement requests are sometimes sensitive and the Team Leads should not have access to the Reimbursement records submitted by the Users in the Call Center Agent role. The Director of Support will require access to all Reimbursement records. The role hierarchy is set as follows: Call Center Agent role reports to Team Lead role, which Reports to the Director of Support. Which steps would the Architect take to ensure proper sharing in this Role Hierarchy structure assuming Private Sharing Setting for the Reimbursement Object?
optionA: Leave the Reimbursement Object in "Deployed" Status and set the Director of Supports Profile to "View All" in the object permissions.
optionB: Use an Approval Process to change the owner of the Reimbursement record upon submission to the Director of Support
optionC: Disable Grant Access Using Hierarchies for the Object and create a Sharing Rule to enable sharing to the Director of Support
optionD: The sharing scenario described will occur without any special configuration choices being made by the Architect
explanation:
Because the Director sits above the Team Leads, the requirement to hide reimbursements from Team Leads while still giving the Director access means you must disable "Grant Access Using Hierarchies" on the object, then add a sharing rule granting the Director access. Setting View All on the Director's profile (A) does not stop the Team Lead from inheriting subordinate records, and the default behavior (D) would expose the records to Team Leads.

https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.security_controlling_access_using_hierarchies.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.security_sharing_rules_owner.htm&type=5&language=en_US

question: Universal Containers has a global 24x7 Salesforce.com implementation that supports Sales, Services, Order Management, and various other parts of their business. They have a nested territory hierarchy, 10,000 sales users, and 20,000 support agents. Territory changes happen daily. The demand for new applications and changes to the platform is high and they follow an agile development methodology and deliver new releases every two weeks on the platform. What Salesforce.com feature would help the system recover from a maintenance restart on Salesforce.com servers?
optionA: Enable Granular Locking on the system.
optionB: Enable Deferred Sharing Rule recalculation.
optionC: Enable Parallel Sharing Rule recalculation.
optionD: Enable Filter -Based Opportunity Territory Assignment.
explanation:
Recovering from a Salesforce service restart is what parallel recalculation buys you, not deferral. Salesforce describes asynchronous parallel recalculation of sharing rules as running "in parallel and asynchronously in the background, which speeds up the process and provides better resilience to site operations such as patches and server restarts" — that resilience is the documented answer to this scenario.
Deferred sharing calculations solve a different problem. They are a planned-maintenance tool: an admin suspends group-membership and sharing-rule processing, makes a batch of role, group and rule changes inside a negotiated window, then resumes and manually kicks off a full recalculation. Nothing about deferral helps an org absorb an unplanned restart — and if calculations are still suspended when one happens, access rights are simply stale until someone resumes them.
Granular locking addresses concurrency between group-maintenance operations, and filter-based opportunity territory assignment is an unrelated Sales feature.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.security_sharing_recalculating_parallel.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.security_sharing_defer_sharing_calculations.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.draes.meta/draes/draes_tools_deferred_sharing_maintenance.htm

corrected.note: Answer moved from Deferred Sharing Rule recalculation to Parallel Sharing Rule Recalculation. Salesforce documents parallel recalculation as providing "better resilience to site operations such as patches and server restarts"; deferral is a planned-maintenance-window tool that suspends calculation and requires a manual full recalculation afterwards. (The resilience wording is carried in the Security Implementation Guide through v240; the current help article describes the same asynchronous parallel behaviour.)

question: Universal Containers has a strict security model enforced through object, field, and row-based security mechanisms. The Architect would like to ensure the security model is being thoroughly tested using Apex automated tests. Which three considerations should be made when using the runAs() method to design Apex until tests?
optionA: runAs() does not enforce user permissions or field-level permissions in test classes
optionB: runAs() can be used inside of test classes to validate record-level security
optionC: runAs() can be used inside of test classes to validate field-level permissions
optionD: runAs() can be used outside of test classes to bypass record-level security
optionE: runAs () counts towards total DML statements issued within transaction
explanation:
Two of the three keyed considerations are solid. runAs can only be used inside a test method, and it is the way a test validates record-level security (B); and "Every call to runAs counts against the total number of DML statements issued in the process" (E). Option D is false for the same reason B is true — runAs is test-only.
Option A is the legacy statement and no longer matches the documentation. Using the runAs Method now says that inside a runAs block "the user's sharing rules and object-level and field-level permissions are enforced", regardless of the test class's sharing mode. On that reading option C — validating field-level permissions — is also true, which makes this a choose-three with four defensible options.
Keep A as the exam key, but know why it is contested: outside runAs, Apex generally runs in system mode and ignores the running user's object and field permissions, which is the fact the option is reaching for. Inside the block, the documentation says those permissions apply.
References:
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_testing_tools_runas.htm
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_classes_perms_enforcing.htm

corrected.note: Key stands, but option A ("runAs does not enforce user permissions or field-level permissions") contradicts the current Apex Developer Guide, which states that object-level and field-level permissions are enforced within a runAs block. That also makes option C arguably true, so the choose-three has four defensible options. Flagged as defective rather than re-keyed, because A is the answer the exam tests.

question: An External Object is created to show Invoices from an external accounting system. When viewing the External Object, a user should only access invoice records the user is authorized to see. What two actions are required to achieve the above requirement? Choose 2 answers
optionA: Setup External Object to use OAuth to connect to the Accounting system.
optionB: Create an owner based sharing rule to grant visibility to the Invoice object.
optionC: Restrict access to data in the accounting system.
optionD: Grant access to the External Object to only the Account Manager profile.
explanation:
External Object rows live in the external system, so per-user authorization is enforced there: connect via OAuth so each user authenticates as themselves (A), and restrict the data in the accounting system itself (C). Salesforce sharing rules (B) and profile grants (D) do not filter external-object rows on a per-record basis.

question: Which three capabilities are available with Enterprise Territory Management? Choose 3 answers
optionA: Create a public group with Territory
optionB: Share a report or dashboard folder with a Territory
optionC: Metadata API Support
optionD: Integration with Collaborative Forecasting
explanation:
All three keyed options are real Enterprise Territory Management capabilities. Salesforce's own comparison of original Territory Management and ETM lists Metadata API Support as No for the original feature and Yes for ETM, Integration with Collaborative Forecasts as No and Yes, and Assignment of Territory on Opportunities as Yes for both (available in ETM since Spring '15).

question: Universal Containers has set up Partner users, who will see records owned by partner users in roles below them in the hierarchy. Which three roles make up the partner role hierarchy?
optionA: Owner, Manager, and User
optionB: Executive, Manager, and Worker
optionC: Executive, Manager, and User
optionD: Administrator, Manager, and User
explanation:
Enabling a partner account creates a three-tier role hierarchy beneath that account — Partner Executive, Partner Manager, and Partner User (C). A partner user sees records owned by partner users at the roles below their own within that account, so an Executive sees Manager- and User-owned records, a Manager sees User-owned records, and a User sees only their own. The other option sets rename or invent tiers that the platform does not create.

question: (Variant) Susan posts a file to the Chatter feed for a record of an object which OWD is private. Which two statements accurately describe who can view the file by default? Choose 2 answers.
optionA: Susan and users with the View All Data permission.
optionB: Susan and users with access to the record.
optionC: Susan and users with a shared chatter post link to the file.
optionD: Susan only.
explanation:
Posting a file to a record's feed puts it in the "Privately Shared" state, and Salesforce spells out who that reaches: "Only the file owner, users with Modify All Data or View All Data permission, and specific file viewers can find and view this file." Records are among the entities that pick up viewer permission — "Groups (including group members) and records have viewer permission for files posted to their feeds" — so anyone with access to the record can see the file.
That makes both A and B correct. The record's Private org-wide default limits who can see the file through the record, but the org-wide View All Data permission reaches it independently.
It is not restricted to Susan alone, and the file does not require a shared post link — link sharing is a separate way of making a file privately shared, not a precondition for this one.

https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?language=en_US&id=sf.collab_files_settings_perms.htm&type=5

question: Universal Containers created a custom object called Defect and would like to enable the Sharing button on the Defect page layout to share the records manually to other users in the organization. In which scenario will the Sharing button appear?
optionA: The Sharing model is either Private or Public Read only.
optionB: The Sharing button always appears.
optionC: The Sharing model is Public Read/Write.
optionD: The Sharing model is Public Read/Write/Transfer.
explanation:
The Sharing button appears only when the object's OWD is more restrictive than Public Read/Write, that is Private or Public Read Only, because manual sharing makes sense only when there is access to grant. Under Public Read/Write everyone already has full access, so the button is not shown, which makes B, C, and D incorrect.

question: A custom ServiceFeedback object is used to collect partner feedback. ServiceFeedback records should be available to all internal employees. The OWD is set to Private for external users so partners cannot see feedback from other partner users. How can the Architect give access to all internal employees?
optionA: Create a trigger on ServiceFeedback to change ownership to an internal employee.
optionB: Ensure all the internal users are above the partners in the role hierarchy.
optionC: Create an Owner based sharing rule for all ServiceFeedback records owned by Partners.
optionD: Set OWD, for Internal Users to Public Read Only.
explanation:
With separate internal and external OWD, you can keep external (partner) access Private so partners cannot see each other's feedback while setting the internal OWD to Public Read Only so all employees can read every ServiceFeedback record. Ownership triggers or sharing rules (A and C), and stacking all internal users in the hierarchy (B), are unnecessary when split OWD solves it directly.

question: Universal Containers (UC) has implemented Customer Community with customer community plus license for its distributors. Retail distributors have part-time agents who work for multiple distributors. Those agents should have access to other distributor accounts as well. What can be configured to grant agents access to different distributor accounts?
optionA: Use Apex sharing to share distributor accounts with agents using the Account__ Share table.
optionB: Use share group to share distributor accounts with agents who have account contact relationship.
optionC: Create sharing rules to share distributor accounts with agents.
optionD: Create sharing set to share distributor accounts with agents using account contact relationship.
explanation:
A sharing set handles the multi-account case directly, and it is the documented mechanism for exactly this shape of problem. Create a Sharing Set for Experience Cloud Site Users covers it: "If you created a user from a contact to multiple accounts, you can grant access to all records with a lookup to any accounts related to that contact. Select Contact.RelatedAccount and Account respectively, and make sure that the relevant account-contact relationships are active."
That is the part-time agent scenario. The agent is one contact related to several distributor accounts through Contacts to Multiple Accounts, and Account is itself an available object in a sharing set, so the access mapping grants each agent the distributor accounts their contact is actively related to. Adding or removing an account-contact relationship changes access with no code.
Apex managed sharing on the account share table would also work, but it is a code solution to a problem the platform already solves declaratively, and it has to be maintained as agents move between distributors. Ordinary sharing rules cannot target community users on a per-account basis.
Note that share groups — a different feature — are the thing unavailable to Customer Community Plus and Partner Community licences. Sharing sets themselves are available.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.networks_setting_light_users.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.users_license_types_communities.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: Answer moved from Apex sharing to the sharing set. The previous explanation claimed a sharing set keyed on the account-contact relationship "only covers the agent's own account"; the sharing-set documentation says the opposite, naming Contact.RelatedAccount as the mapping for a contact related to multiple accounts.

question: Universal Containers has developed an AppExchange managed package for their distribution partners, which required a private key to be generated for each partner and used by the code. Universal Containers support representatives must be able to access the private key value to debug connection issues, but it must not be possible for the partner to access the value. How can the Architect best support this requirement?
optionA: Store the value in a text field on a protected custom setting in the package.
optionB: Store the value in a static variable in a class included in the managed package.
optionC: Store the value in the text field on a list custom setting in the managed package.
optionD: Store the value in an encrypted field on a custom object in the package.
explanation:
The discriminator here is that support representatives must be able to read the value, not merely that partners must not. That rules out the storage that would otherwise be the obvious choice: in a managed package a protected custom setting is reachable only by Apex inside that package and namespace, and the subscriber cannot read it at all — which hides the key from support staff working in the partner org just as effectively as from the partner.
An encrypted field on a packaged custom object keeps the value retrievable while masking it by default: only users with the View Encrypted Data permission see the plain text, and it is masked for everyone else. Grant that permission to the support profile and withhold it from partner profiles and both halves of the requirement are met. A list custom setting protects nothing, and a static variable is not stored data you can look at later.
Worth stating plainly, because the protection is only as good as the permission hygiene: whoever administers the subscriber org can in principle assign View Encrypted Data, so this design relies on that permission being controlled. Where the value must never be readable by the subscriber at all, protected custom settings or protected custom metadata in a managed package are the stronger option — which is why the related "how do I secure callout credentials" item keys those instead.

question: Universal Containers has created a custom object to store highly confidential client relationship data with Private sharing settings. Which two options would an Architect choose to ensure access only to the record owner and the administrator? Choose 2 answers.

optionB: Disable the "Create" permission on all other profiles.
optionC: Disable the "Read" permission on all other profiles.

explanation:

question: Universal Containers has a customer that meets criteria for two Enterprise territory Management territories (Portugal and Southern Europe). What is necessary to assign opportunities to a territory for this account?
optionA: Create a criteria-based sharing rule on the Opportunity to assign It to a territory.
optionB: Create a Process Builder Process that updates the Territory field on the Opportunity
optionC: The territory with the highest Territory Type Priority is automatically assigned to the Opportunity
optionD: Create an Apex class that implement. Filter-Based Opportunity Territory Assignment

question: Universal Containers has a Performance Feedback custom object (Private organization-wide default) used by customers to report any Issues with delivery drivers. Feedback should not be visible to the driver, but any feedback records should be accessible to people above them in the Role Hierarchy, even when the driver changes managers. Assuming managers have Read access to the Feedback object, which three steps are necessary to solve these requirements?
optionA: Remove Read permission on the Driver profile, have feedback ownership transferred to the driver's manager when feedback Is submitted, and use the Role Hierarchy to give access to a driver's manager.
optionB: Remove Read permission on the Driver profile, have feedback ownership transferred to the driver when feedback is submitted, and use the Role Hierarchy to give access to a driver's manager.
optionC: Remove Read permission on the Driver profile, have feedback ownership transferred to the driver when feedback is submitted, and create an ownership-based sharing rule,
explanation:
Feedback must be hidden from the driver yet visible to managers even as managers change, so keep the driver as owner (so the dynamic Role Hierarchy always routes access to whoever is currently above them) and remove Read on the Driver profile so the owner still cannot see it. An ownership-based sharing rule (C, the source answer) is static and breaks when the manager changes, and transferring ownership to the manager (A) loses the driver linkage.

question: What should a Salesforce architect recommend to make sure that users that gained access to a custom of sharing do not lose access to it when its owner is changed?
optionA: Create a specific Sharing Reason for the custom object.
optionB: Use ''runAS'' system method in Apex classes to enforce record visibility.
optionC: Create a new record in the Share object with RowCause "Manual".
optionD: Use ''With Sharing'' keyword to make sure record visibility will be considered
explanation:
Apex managed sharing rows tagged with a custom Apex Sharing Reason are preserved when record ownership changes, whereas "Manual" row-cause shares (C) are deleted on owner change. The runAs and "With Sharing" options (B and D) are unrelated to whether a share row persists.

question: Universal Containers has a custom object, Employee Review, with an Organization-Wide Default security setting of Private. A user lookup on the Employee Review object is populated when a reviewer is assigned to perform a review. How can this user be granted edit access to the record if they are not the owner?
optionA: The user will be granted access to the record automatically when the user lookup is populated.
optionB: Create a workflow rule to share the Employee Review record with the user in the lookup field.
optionC: Create an Apex trigger to insert an Employee Review Share record with an access level of Edit.
optionD: Create a criteria-based sharing rule to share the record with the user in the lookup field.
explanation:
A user named in a lookup needs edit access on a private record, which requires programmatic Apex managed sharing; a trigger inserts an EmployeeReview share row at access level Edit for that user. Populating a lookup does not grant access (A), workflow cannot create share records (B), and a criteria-based rule cannot target the arbitrary user in the lookup (D).

question: Assuming granular locking is enabled, what activity can happen in parallel to changing a community account owner without risking group membership lock errors?
optionA: Deletion of a Role
optionB: Creation of a Role
optionC: Creation of a Territory
optionD: Deletion of a Territory
explanation:
Salesforce publishes the concurrency matrix for granular locking, and the row for this scenario is unambiguous: "Changing customer or partner account owner — Territory creation." That single entry is the whole answer; territory creation is the only listed operation that can proceed alongside it.
Role creation, role deletion and territory deletion all appear elsewhere in the table but not in this row, because changing the owner of a customer or partner account is a form of role reparenting — the partner account's roles move to a new parent — and reparenting still blocks almost all other group updates.
