https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.draes.meta/draes/draes_group_membership_locking.htm

question: A banking company wants their customers Date of Birth Field searchable by Banking Reps, but only editable by Customer Support Reps. Which approach is recommended to meet this requirement?
optionA: Create a Validation rule on the Date of Birth field so the rule returns true only when user.profilename matches Customer Support Rep.
optionB: Set the Field-Level Security for the Date of Birth field to be Visible to the Customer Support Rep profile, and set the Date of Birth field Visible and Read-Only to the Banking Rep profile.
optionC: Add Date of Birth field to the Search layout of the Contact Object. Modify the Page layout assigned to Customer Support Rep and add Date of Birth field as Required.
explanation:
Field-Level Security is the declarative way to make the Date of Birth field searchable and visible to Banking Reps as read-only while keeping it editable for Customer Support Reps. A validation rule (A) blocks save but does not cleanly control visibility and edit, and requiring the field on a layout (C) does not restrict who may edit it.

question: When you make changes to roles and groups, Salesforce locks the entire group membership table, which makes it impossible to process group changes in multiple threads to increase throughput on updates. Which feature should be enabled to address this?
optionA: Deferred Sharing Maintenance
optionB: Granular Locking
optionC: Parallel Sharing Rule Recalculation
optionD: Implicit Sharing
explanation:
Granular locking replaces the single lock over the entire group-membership table with locks scoped to the parts of the membership graph actually being touched, which is what allows concurrent processing. Salesforce lists the benefits: groups in separate hierarchies can be manipulated concurrently, public groups and roles that do not include territories are not blocked by territory operations, users can be added to territories and public groups at the same time, and user provisioning can run in parallel.
The other three are different features. Deferred sharing maintenance suspends recalculation for a planned window rather than parallelising it; parallel sharing rule recalculation speeds up sharing-rule recalculation specifically, not group-membership updates; and implicit sharing is built-in record access between accounts and their children, not a concurrency control.
Note that granular locking is enabled by default in current orgs — the stem describes the pre-granular-locking behaviour.
References:
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.draes.meta/draes/draes_group_membership_locking.htm

optionD: The "Manager" Report folder permission.

question: Universal Containers (UC) has a business unit that uses a custom object to track requests which demands a high level of internal team collaboration. Although all requests must have an owner, all employees are required to collaborate on requests. Which recommendation should a Salesforce architect provide to optimize the solution and meet these requirements?
optionA: Set the Request object's OWD to Public Read/Write.
optionB: Set the Request object's OWD to Private and grant Modify All Data permission on all Profiles for the Request object.
optionC: Set the Request object's OWD to Private and criteria-based sharing rule to share all Request records with all internal users.
optionD: Set the Request object's OWD to Public Read Only and configure role hierarchy.
explanation:
When every employee must read and edit requests while each record still has an owner, the simplest optimal model is OWD Public Read/Write, which retains ownership but lets all users collaborate. Modify All Data (B) over-grants across the platform, and a rule sharing to all internal users (C) is heavier than simply opening the OWD.

https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.security_sharing_owd_about.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Which two access grants are stored in the Group Maintenance tables? Choose 2 answers
optionA: Inherited access grants
optionB: Explicit grants
optionC: Group Membership grants
optionD: Implicit grants
explanation:
Salesforce uses four types of access grant — explicit, group membership, inherited and implicit — and splits them across two families of table. Record-Level Access: Under the Hood defines the Group Maintenance tables as "Tables that store the data supporting group membership and inherited access grants", which is options C and A.
The division of labour is worth holding onto: the Object Sharing table records grants made to a particular user or group on a particular record, while the Group Maintenance tables record who belongs to which group and who therefore inherits from whom. A query joins the two — record id against Object Sharing, then user or group id against Group Maintenance — so an explicit grant to one user resolves at runtime into access for everyone above them.
Explicit grants live in the Object Sharing table, and implicit grants are maintained by the system on the objects themselves, so neither belongs in the Group Maintenance tables.
References:
https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/salesforce_record_access_under_the_hood.pdf

question: Universal Containers (UC) has 200 distributors that use Partner Community Licenses. Partners cannot see each other's data, but UC is also trying to give more visibility to certain individuals at a distributor. Which scalable solution would an architect recommend that will give users in the partner manager role access to all Case and Container records owned by other partner managers and partner users (but not the partner executive) at the same distributor?
optionA: Create Sharing sets.
optionB: Create a permission set granting the View All permission to Case and Container records.
optionC: Give Super User permission to the partner manager users.
optionD: Create ownership-based sharing rules for your distributors.
explanation:
Super user access is the feature built for this, and it scales because it is granted per user rather than configured per distributor. Salesforce describes it for Partner Community licences as letting a user "get insights into the records of other partner users who are at their role level or below them in the account role hierarchy", covering cases, leads, custom objects and opportunities.
That maps onto the requirement exactly. Each partner account has its own Partner User, Partner Manager and Partner Executive hierarchy, so a partner manager with super user access reaches records owned by other partner managers and by partner users at the same distributor, and stops short of the partner executive above them.
Ownership-based sharing rules would need one rule per distributor across 200 accounts, and a View All permission set would expose every case and container in the org rather than one distributor's.

question: The sales manager in Japan have asked the sales manager in Australia to assist them with closing their deals. How are these requirements achieved?
optionA: Use sharing set to give the sales manager access to the deals.
optionB: Create ownership-based sharing rule.
optionC: Use opportunity teams to automatically add the sales manager as a team member.
optionD: Assign the sales manager View All on the opportunity object.
explanation:
The Australia manager needs access to the Japan team's deals, so an ownership-based sharing rule sharing opportunities owned by the Japan managers to the Australia manager grants it declaratively. A sharing set (A) is community-only and View All (D) over-grants. Opportunity teams (C) are arguably cleaner for purely ad-hoc help, so this is worth noting.

question: Universal Containers (UC) has a private Organization-Wide Defaults (OWD) model for the Account object and needs to control the access of records and fields according to these requirements: * Sales reps can view/edit only their own records and cannot access the field "segment" in account page. * Service reps need to view all accounts but cannot edit any information. * Sales managers can modify any account of reps reporting to them. * Service managers can modify any account. How can a Salesforce architect provide an optimal solution for this scenario?
optionA: Use profiles, sharing rules, and change OWD to public read-only.
optionB: Use profiles, manual sharing, and field-level security.
optionC: Use profiles, permission sets, and field-level security.
optionD: Use profiles, permission sets, role hierarchy, and field-level security.
explanation:
The mixed requirements of own versus all, edit versus view, manager-modifies-reports, and hiding a field require the full stack: profiles and permission sets for object access, role hierarchy for the manager-edit rule, and Field-Level Security to hide the segment field. Options that omit role hierarchy or FLS (A, B, and C) cannot satisfy both the manager-edit and the field-hiding requirements.

question: Universal Containers regularly uploads large amounts of parent and child records into Salesforce to maintain integrations with other systems that update their date in scheduled batches or continuously in real time. Which two situations may pose a risk of producing locking errors? Choose 2 answers.
optionA: Updates to child records that have the same parent records are being processed simultaneously in separate transactions.
optionB: Updates to parent and child records are being processed in the same batch.
optionC: Updates to parent records and their child records being processed simultaneously in separate threads.
optionD: Updates to parent and child records are being processed synchronously in the same threads.
explanation:
Lock contention arises when related parent and child rows are updated concurrently in separate transactions or threads, because Salesforce locks the parent during the child's sharing and rollup operations. Processing parent and child together in the same batch or synchronously in the same thread (B and D) serializes the work and avoids the lock.
References:
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.draes.meta/draes/draes_object_relationships_record_level_locking.htm

question: A dummy user at Universal Containers owns more that 10,000 lead records. The system assigned all these leads to a dummy user. This is causing performance issues whenever role hierarchy changes. Which two options should be recommended to improve performance? Choose 2 answers.
optionA: Assign ownership to a small number of users.
optionB: Add the dummy user into a public group.
optionC: Add the dummy user to the bottom of the role hierarchy.
optionD: Do not assign a role to the dummy user.
explanation:
Ownership data skew is "when a single user owns more than 10,000 records of an object", and Salesforce gives two remedies for the parked-leads pattern in this stem. The first is to spread the records: "Distributing ownership of records across a greater number of users decreases the chance of long-running updates occurring." The second is the one that applies when you must keep a dummy owner: "If you do have a compelling reason for assigning ownership to a small number of users, you can minimize possible performance impacts by not assigning the users to a role" — which is option D exactly.
Option A is the intended "spread the ownership out" answer, but read it as printed and it says the opposite of the documentation, which names assigning ownership to a small number of users as the risky configuration rather than the fix. Treat A as loosely worded rather than as a rule to memorise.
The two rejected options are wrong for specific documented reasons. Salesforce says to keep skewed owners out of public groups that can be the source of a sharing rule, so B makes things worse; and where such a user must have a role, the guidance is to place them in a separate role at the top of the hierarchy and leave them there, not at the bottom, so C is backwards too.
References:
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.draes.meta/draes/draes_group_membership_data_skew.htm

corrected.note: Answer stands, but option A as printed inverts the documented remedy — Salesforce prescribes distributing ownership across a greater number of users and describes "assigning ownership to a small number of users" as the condition that causes skew. The old explanation read A as "distributing ownership across many users", which is not what the option says.

question: Universal Container (UC) wants all full-time internal employees to be able to view all leads. A subset of employees should also be able to see leads. Which organization default (OWD) approach should an architect recommend that will help US implement these requirement?
optionA: Implement a Public Read/write OWD on Lead
optionB: Implement a Public Read only OWD on Lead
optionC: Implement a Public Read/write/Transfer OWD on Lead.
optionD: Implement a Private OWD on Lead.
explanation:
Public Read Only gives every internal employee visibility of every lead while keeping edit rights with the owner, which is the baseline this requirement needs. A subset can then be granted edit through sharing rules layered on top — org-wide defaults set the floor, and sharing rules are the exceptions that open access further.
Private would hide leads from everyone but their owners, which is the opposite of "all employees can view all leads". Public Read/Write and Public Read/Write/Transfer hand edit, and in the second case transfer, to the whole org, which over-grants.
(The stem looks garbled: its second sentence repeats "see leads" where the requirement it is contrasting must be edit access. Read it as "a subset of employees should also be able to edit leads" — that is the only reading on which the four options differ meaningfully.)
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.security_sharing_owd_about.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers has set Account Sharing to Private with Account Teams enabled. Which two user groups can add team members on the Account? Choose 2 answers
optionA: The current Account Owner can add team members.
optionB: The user specified as the Manager on the Owner's User record
optionC: Someone above the Account Owner in the Role Hierarchy with read access
optionD: Any Account Team Member with read access on the Account
explanation:
Account Team members can be added by the current account owner (A) and by users above the owner in the Role Hierarchy who have read access to the account (C). The owner's "Manager" user-record field (B) is irrelevant to sharing, and existing team members themselves (D) cannot add others.

question: Universal Containers has the following requirements: * The Commercial Account and Consumer Account support departments should not collaborate. * The Commercial and Consumer sales users roll up to the same VP of Sales, but there should be no collaboration between sales departments. * The Commercial sales department should share its customers with the Commercial support department. * The Consumer sales department shares its customers with the Consumer support department. * The Commercial and Consumer support departments roll up to the same Support Director. * The sales departments will remain the Account Owner for the Accounts that they sell to. What is the recommended Org-Wide Sharing Default for Accounts, and how would the Architect enable proper Commercial and Consumer Sales to Support Account Sharing for this scenario?
optionA: Private Account Sharing with Sharing Rules from Commercial Sales Role(s) to Consumer Support Role(s) and Consumer Sales Role(s) to Commercial Support Role(s).
optionB: Private Account Sharing with Sharing Rules from Commercial support Role(s) to Commercial Support Role(s) and Consumer Sales Role(s) to Consumer Support Role(s).
optionC: Read-Only Account Sharing with Sharing Rules from Commercial Sales Role(s) to Consumer Support Group(s) and Consumer Sales Role(s) to Commercial Support Groups(s).
optionD: Private Account Sharing with Sharing Rules from Commercial Sales Group(s) to Commercial Support Groups(s) and Consumer Sales Group(s) to Consumer Support Group(s).
explanation:
The sales departments stay owners under a Private model, and group-to-group sharing rules mapping each Sales group to its matching Support group give each support team only its own department's accounts with no cross-collaboration. The cross-matched mappings (A and C) would share to the wrong department, and B's role-based wording does not correctly isolate the departments.

question: Universal Containers (UC) has created a public group with certain Sales Engineers to help on complex deals and a sharing rule to grant access to these opportunities. Opportunity OWD is private. What is the impact of these sharing settings?
optionA: Subordinates of Managers who have Sales Engineers in the public group will also have access to these records.
optionB: Sales Engineers that have a similar role of the Sales Engineers of the public group will also have access to these records.
optionC: Sales Engineers Managers and their managers in the role hierarchy will also have access to these records.
optionD: Sales Engineers direct reports will also have access to these records.
explanation:
Sharing to a public group grants access to the group's members and, through the Role Hierarchy, to users above those members, so the Sales Engineers' managers and their managers also gain access to the opportunities. Subordinates, similar-role peers, and direct reports (A, B, and D) do not inherit a group-based share.

question: Universal Containers has recently activated an integration that synchronizes customer information and orders into their CRM of choice: Salesforce.com. One of their largest customers, United Air, has over 12,000 unique contacts. Since the integration was activated, sales reps are having trouble adding contacts to the United Air account. When a sales rep adds a contact, they get the following error message: UNABLE_TO_LOCK_ROW, this issue seems to affect the United Air account and several other large customers. The sales rep can usually save the contact by trying again later in the evening. What should the Architect recommend as a possible solution?
optionA: Add a role-based sharing rule so all sales team members have Read/Write access to contacts.
optionB: Remove sharing rules and replace them with Apex sharing for Unite Air and the other large accounts.
optionC: Implement an account hierarchy and redistribute the contacts evenly under the child accounts.
optionD: Create a permission set for the sales team to grant them Read/Write access to all account fields.
explanation:
The UNABLE_TO_LOCK_ROW error on a 12,000-contact account is parent (lookup) data skew, where too many child contacts under one account cause lock contention; redistributing the contacts across child accounts in an account hierarchy relieves it. Sharing-rule changes (A and B) or a field-access permission set (D) do not address the parent-row locking.
References:
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.draes.meta/draes/draes_object_relationships_parent_child_data_skew.htm

question: At Universal Containers, users should only see Accounts they or their subordinates own. All Accounts with the custom field "Kay Customer" should be visible to all Senior Account Managers. There is a custom field on the Account record that contains sensitive information and should be hidden from all users, except 3 designated users who require view and edit access. These three users come from different user groups, and will change occasionally. Which three platform security features are required to support these requirements with the minimum amount of effort? Choose 3 answers
optionA: Criteria-Based Sharing Rules
optionB: Owner-Based Sharing Rules
optionC: Role Hierarchy
optionD: Apex Managed Sharing
explanation:
The owner-or-subordinates visibility comes from the Role Hierarchy under a Private model (C), the Key Customer visibility for all Senior Account Managers is a criteria-based sharing rule (A), and the sensitive field for three rotating cross-group users is best handled with a Permission Set granting FLS (E). Owner-based rules (B) and Apex managed sharing (D) add unnecessary effort for these requirements.
References:

https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.users_profiles_field_perms.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers is a fast-growing company that sells containers globally. It has thousands of dealerships throughout the world where local dealers service Containers sold locally. They recently opened two dealerships in California: NorthCal and SoCal. Universal Containers implemented a new partner community to enable their dealers. Each dealership has a dealer Manager who has all service agents report into them. Assuming a private sharing model, what is the best option to enable dealer managers to have visibility to customer cases within their dealership and not across all dealerships?
optionA: Create sharing groups that share all cases to all agents under the Dealer manager.
optionB: Create a batch job that creates sharing rules as needed, based on the cases created.
optionC: Build a trigger that create manual sharing of cases as needed whenever a new case is created.
optionD: No changes are needed to the sharing and visibility model to implement this requirement.
explanation:
In a private partner community, the dealer manager already sits above their service agents in the Role Hierarchy per dealership, so cases owned by agents are visible to their own manager and not across dealerships with no extra configuration. Sharing groups, batch jobs, or triggers (A, B, and C) are redundant given the hierarchy.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.networks_partner_roles_overview.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Sales Reps at Universal Containers sometimes create large files as a part of the Sales process that are too large to share over email. They would like users to be able to share files with customers, but the CISO has requested that any file links shared must be protected by a password. How can this be accomplished?
optionA: Set up an experience cloud site for customers to access files. Share the file with customers via chatter. Customers can then log into the site to access the content.
optionB: Sales reps can create a content delivery. During creation, the user should select the option to require a password to access content.
optionC: Utilize an AppExchange product for delivering password-protected files to their customers,
explanation:
Salesforce Content Delivery lets a rep generate a shareable link for a large file and, at creation, require a password to access it, meeting the CISO's requirement natively. An Experience Cloud site (A) is heavier and a site login is not a per-file password, and an AppExchange product (C) is unnecessary for a built-in capability.

https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.content_delivery_about.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A sales rep at Universal Containers (UC) has manually shared an Opportunity record with internal Pre-Sales users. After some time, the sales rep moved to another position and all opportunities records that were owned were transferred to a new sales rep. What happened to the internal Pre-Sales users' access to the opportunity?
optionA: They still have access to the record due to inherited sharing.
optionB: They still have access to the record due to implicit sharing.
optionC: They will no longer have access to the record.
optionD: They still have access to the record due to team access.
explanation:
A manual share is deleted when record ownership changes, so when the opportunity is transferred to a new rep the Pre-Sales users' manually granted access is removed. That access is not preserved by implicit, inherited, or team mechanisms (A, B, and D), because none of those created the share.

question: Universal Containers would like to create a custom team solution that can be used on a custom Loan object. The following requirements must be met: The Loan custom object should be set to Private in the Org-Wide Defaults. Any user added to the Custom Team object should have Read Only access to the corresponding Loan record. If the Custom Team record is marked as "Primary" then the corresponding user should have Read/Edit access to the corresponding Loan record. Which two methods will allow the Architect to meet the requirements? Choose 2 answers.
optionA: Create a custom trigger on the Custom Team object that inserts or updates records in the Loan_share object.
optionB: Create a criteria-based sharing rule on the Loan object that will share the Loan record with the appropriate user in the Custom Team object.
optionC: Create Apex Sharing Reasons on the Loan object to identify the reason the Loan record was share.
optionD: Create an owner-based sharing rule on the Custom Team object that will share the Loan record to the owner of the Custom Team record.
explanation:
Differential access of Read for members and Read/Edit for the Primary record on a private object requires Apex managed sharing: a trigger writes Loan share rows at the correct access level (A), and defining Apex Sharing Reasons identifies and maintains those shares and preserves them on owner change (C). A criteria-based rule (B) cannot read the related Custom Team's Primary flag per record, and an owner-based rule (D) shares to the wrong target.

question: Universal Containers would like to restrict users' access to export reports What option supports this requirement?
optionA: Remove the "Report Manager" user permission.
optionB: Remove the Export button from the report page layout.
optionC: Remove "Allow Export" on the report folder settings.
optionD: Remove the "Export Reports" profile permission.
explanation:

question: Which two reasons should the Architect consider regarding the use of Apex Sharing Reasons? Choose 2 answers
optionA: Ensuring the developer can more easily troubleshoot programmatic sharing.
optionB: Ensuring the Share record is not deleted upon ownership change.
optionC: Ensuring the Share record is deleted upon ownership change.
optionD: Ensuring there is additional criteria available for Criteria-Based Sharing.
explanation:
Apex Sharing Reasons label programmatic shares so developers can identify and troubleshoot why a record was shared (A), and shares created with a custom reason are retained when ownership changes, unlike Manual shares (B). They do not delete shares on owner change (C) and do not add criteria to criteria-based sharing (D).

question: Universal Containers has Controlled by Parent sharing settings on the Contact object and Public Read Only sharing settings on Account, Opportunity, and Case objects. Which two options can the user see while adding Account team members to the Account?
optionA: Case Access
optionB: Opportunity Access
optionC: Contact Access
optionD: Activity Access

question: Universal Container is creating a custom VF page to allow user to edit contact records. The developer has used an apex:outputField for the Phone field on the contact obj. What is the expected behavior if a user without FLS accesses the VF page?

explanation:

question: Universal Containers (UC) service reps are assigned to a profile which has View All on the Case object (Private OWD). To make sure service reps have access to all relevant information to attend to customer requests, which two details should Salesforce Architects consider? Choose 2 answers.
optionA: Service reps will be able to access all UC contact records if they are controlled by parent.
optionB: Service reps will not be able to access all UC contact records if they are controlled by parent.
optionC: Service reps will be able to access all the UC Account records due to Implicit Sharing.
optionD: Service reps will not be able to access all the UC Account records because Account OWD is private.
explanation:
View All on Case opens up cases and nothing else, and the detail that decides this item is a documented exception to implicit sharing. Salesforce grants read-only access to a parent account to a user who has access to a child case, contact or opportunity — but the same table lists among that behaviour's conditions: "Not granted by the View All permission on the child object."
So the service reps see every case, and still see no accounts, because the Account org-wide default is Private and their case access came from a permission rather than from sharing (D). Contacts controlled by their parent inherit the account's access, so those stay invisible too (B).
That is also why C is wrong even though it sounds like the standard implicit-sharing rule: implicit parent access is exactly what View All does not trigger.
References:
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.draes.meta/draes/draes_object_relationships_implicit_sharing.htm

question: For the Universal Containers Commercial and Consumer support departments, having access to Activities for Contacts with which they interact is important. Commercial support users should not see Consumer Accounts/Contacts and Consumer support users should not see Commercial Accounts/Contacts. Assuming the Organization-Wide Default for Activities is set to "Controlled by Parent" what is the minimum level of Sharing access a support user would need to Accounts/Contacts to view associated Activities?
optionA: Private Account/Contact Sharing Default with a Sharing Rule for each department set to Public Read/Write access to Accounts/Contacts.
optionB: Private Account/Contact Sharing Default with a Sharing Rule for each department set to Private access to Accounts/Contacts.
optionC: The users need no access to Accounts/Contacts with the proper Activity Sharing Rules and Profile Permissions for the Accounts Tab.
optionD: Private Account/Contact Sharing Default with a Sharing Rule for each department set to Public Read only access to Accounts/Contacts.
explanation:
With Activities set to Controlled by Parent, a user needs at least Read on the parent Account or Contact to see its activities, so keep Accounts and Contacts Private and grant each department Read-only through sharing rules to keep commercial and consumer data separated. Read/Write (A) over-grants, and "no access" to accounts and contacts (C) cannot satisfy Controlled-by-Parent activity visibility.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.security_sharing_owd_about.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal containers (UC) implemented a private organization-wide default for the Container and Case objects. How can UC give support representatives access to Container and Case records owned by Customer Community users?
optionA: Create an ownership-based sharing rule that gives access to the head of support role and internal subordinates
optionB: Create a criteria-based sharing rule that gives access to the head of support role and internal subordinates

question: Universal Containers (UC) is implementing Sales Cloud. During the last quarter of the financial year, they requested a solution in Salesforce to allow them to specify an assistance agent on the opportunity via an assistant field. The system should automatically remove access from the previous assistant when the field changes. What is the optimum solution to meet the requirements?

question: Universal Containers is implementing a community of High-Volume Community users. Community users should be able to see records associated to their Account or Contact record. The Architect is planning to use a Sharing Set to provide access to the records. When setting up the Sharing Set, certain objects are not available in the list of Available Objects. Which two reasons explain why an object is excluded from the list of Available Objects in a Sharing Set?
optionA: The object is a custom object, and therefore not available for a sharing set.
optionB: The object's Organization-Wide sharing setting is set to Public Read/Write.
optionC: The object's Organization-Wide sharing setting is set to Private.
optionD: The custom object does not have a lookup to Accounts or Contacts.
explanation:
The sharing-set setup page names its own exclusions, and they are exactly the two keyed options. "The Available Objects list excludes: Objects with an org-wide sharing setting of Public Read/Write" and "Custom objects that don't have an account or contact lookup field."
Both exclusions follow from what a sharing set does. It grants site users access to records associated with the account or contact that matches their own, so a custom object with no account or contact lookup gives the access mapping nothing to follow; and an object already open to everyone has no access left to grant.
Custom objects as a class are not excluded — they appear in the supported list — and Private is the setting sharing sets exist to extend, not a disqualifier.

question: Universal Containers (UC) has a requirement to expose a web service to their business partners. The web service will be used to allow each business partner to query UC's Salesforce instance to retrieve the status of orders. The business partner should only be allowed access to orders for which the business partner is the fulfillment vendor. The Architect does not want the business partners to utilize the standard APIs and would prefer a custom API be developed. Which three design elements should the Architect consider in order to ensure the data security of the solution? Choose 3 answers
optionA: Query the Orders object with Dynamic SOQL based upon the fulfillment ID.
optionB: Set the Orders object's sharing settings to Private in the Org-Wide Defaults
optionC: Provide each partner with their own Salesforce login set to API Enabled on the profile.
optionD: Develop a custom Apex web service with a fulfillment ID input attribute
optionE: Develop a custom Apex web service using the "With Sharing" keyword.
explanation:
Data security for the partner web service comes from a Private Orders OWD (B), a "with sharing" Apex service that respects the running user's access (E), and filtering the SOQL by the partner's fulfillment ID (A). Per-partner logins (C) and a fulfillment-ID input parameter (D) do not themselves enforce row-level security and could be spoofed.

question: Universal Containers has the following requirements: A custom Loan object requires Org-Wide Defaults set to Private. The owner of the Loan record will be the Loan Origination Officer. The Loan record must be shared with a specific Underwriter on a loan-by-loan basis. The Underwriters should only see the Loan records for which they are assigned. What should the Architect recommend to meet these requirements?
optionA: Use criteria-based sharing rules to share the Loan object with the Underwriter based upon the criteria defined in the criteria-based sharing
optionB: Create a lookup relationship from the Loan object to the User object. Use a trigger on the Loan object to create the corresponding record in the Loan share object
optionC: Create a master-detail relationship from the Loan to the User object. Loan records will be automatically shared with the Underwriter
optionD: Create an Apex Sharing Reason on the Loan object that shares the Loan with the Underwriter based upon the criteria defined in the Sharing Reason
explanation:
Per-loan assignment to a specific underwriter, who is an arbitrary user, requires Apex managed sharing: add a User lookup on the Loan and a trigger that inserts the corresponding Loan share row for the assigned underwriter. A master-detail to User (C) is not allowed and would not auto-share, and a criteria-based rule (A) cannot target an arbitrary per-record user.

question: Universal Containers has a Private Sharing Model and restrictive data access settings in place. The data governance team is planning to deploy a master data management tool that will need write access to all system data, and the Architect has been asked to prepare a Data Governance User Profile that has full access to all data regardless of Sharing and CRUD Settings. question: Which users have access to Opportunity records owned by an external user, assuming no other changes to the sharing model have been implemented?
optionA: The record owner and any user above the external user in the role hierarchy.
optionB: The record owner only.
optionC: The record owner and any user below the external user in the role hierarchy.
optionD: The record owner and all internal users.

question: Universal Containers is updating its Organization-Wide Sharing Settings for the Account Object from a "Public Read/Write" model to a "Private" model, so that they can hide certain national accounts from sales reps and sales managers. These national accounts should only be accessible by sales directors and above. Universal Container's Role Hierarchy matches its organizational hierarchy. Which two options should the Architect consider when designing the solution? Choose 2 answers
optionA: Sales directors will need a sharing rule created so that they can see accounts owned by Sales Users.
optionB: National accounts must be owned by a user who is above the sales managers in the Role Hierarchy.
optionC: Apex managed sharing will have to be disabled for the account object to protect the national accounts.
optionD: If a sales rep is added to the Opportunity Team for a national account, they will gain access to account data.
explanation:
To hide national accounts from reps and managers under a Private model, those accounts must be owned by someone above the managers in the hierarchy so the managers do not inherit them (B), and note the side effect that adding a rep to a national account's Opportunity Team grants implicit access to the account (D). Sales directors do not need a special rule to see subordinate-owned accounts (A, since the hierarchy handles it), and disabling Apex sharing (C) is not required.

question: Universal Containers has junction object called "Job Production Facility", with 2 master-detail relationships to the Job and Production Facility custom objects. Both master records have a private sharing model. What statement is true if a user's profile allows access (Create/Read) to the Job, but no access to the Production Facility Object?
optionA: The user will be granted read access to the Production Facility record
optionB: The user will see the junction object and the link to the Production Facility.
optionC: The user will see the junction object but not the link to the Production Facility.
optionD: The user will not be able to see the junction object records or the field values.
explanation:
Custom Object Security states the rule for junction objects directly. For an object on the detail side of a master-detail relationship, viewing a record requires "Read permission and read access to the related master record. If the record has two master records in a many-to-many relationship, the user must have read access to both master records."
This user has no access to Production Facility at all, so the second condition fails and the junction records are invisible — not partially visible, and not visible minus a link. Detail records also inherit their security from their masters and cannot be permissioned independently, so there is no way to grant the junction on its own.
Access in this direction never flows upward either: seeing a junction record would not have granted read on the Production Facility parent, so A is wrong even in the case where the user could see the junction.

question: Sales managers want their team members to help each other close Opportunities. The Opportunity and Account organization-wide defaults are private. To grant Opportunity access to sales reps on the same team, owner ship-based sharing rules were created for each team. What is the side effect of this approach?
optionA: All sales reps will have Read access to Accounts for all Opportunities.

optionC: Sales reps on the same team will have Read access to the Accounts for Opportunities owned by their team members.

question: Universal Containers has implemented a community for its customers using the Customer Community sense type. They have implemented a custom object to store service requests that has a look up to the account record. The Organization Wide Default External Access for the service request object is set to Private. Universal Containers wants their customers to be able to see service requests for their account through the community Customers should not see service requests for other accounts. What Salesforce feature can the Architect use to implement this?
optionA: Use manual sharing to share the service requests manually when a new community user is added.
optionB: Use a Sharing Set to share service requests related to the account based on the community user's profile.
optionC: Use a Sharing Rule to share service requests to the community user based on their role.
optionD: Use Apex Managed Sharing to share service requests related to the account to the appropriate community users.

optionB: Run a Report on Sharing in the Admin Console.
optionC: Log in as each user and Run the All Accounts List View.

question: Universal Containers has a custom Job object with a private sharing model. Based on the size and location of the Job, different teams must have access to edit the specific Job record. To support this requirement, Apex Managed Sharing has been implemented to share records with the required users. Since the teams change frequently, managed sharing recalculations need to be manually run frequently. What can the Architect do to optimize this process?
optionA: Change the sharing model on the Job object to Public Read/Write.
optionB: Create a scheduled job to automatically run the sharing recalculations on a nightly basis.
optionC: Create public groups for each team, and share the jobs with the groups instead of users.
optionD: Create a custom Visualforce page to edit the jobs and specify Without Sharing on the controller.

Opening the OWD (A) removes security, a nightly recalculation job (B) still incurs the recalculation cost, and a without-sharing Visualforce page (D) bypasses security.

question: Universal Containers has just deployed a change to its role hierarchy. A manager is reporting that their staff can now see Accounts that they do not own and should not have access to. How should the Architect troubleshoot?
optionA: While logged in as the System Administrator, use the Field Accessibility Viewer to view a matrix of who has access to Accounts.
optionB: While logged in as the one of the Staff members, navigate to a sample account and use the Sharing button to determine who has access.
optionC: While logged in as the one of the Staff members, navigate to their user record and inspect their profile and role membership.
optionD: While logged in as the System Administrator, review the organization-wide default settings for the Account object under Sharing Settings.

question: After setting up Customer Community and enabling collaboration, the architect realizes that customers can only see Chatter posts from other customers in their account. What should the architect do to allow viewing Chatter posts from all customers?
optionA: Enable Community User Visibility.
optionB: Set View All for Chatter posts.
optionC: Enable Chatter Super User.
optionD: Enable Internal Users Visibility.
explanation:
What the customers are experiencing is the default, and the setting that widens it is Site User Visibility. Salesforce separates the two behaviours: Portal User Visibility means "portal users in the same customer or partner portal account can see each other", which is precisely the "only people in my own account" symptom; Site User Visibility "controls whether user sharing is available for authenticated users in your org's sites", and enabling it exposes the per-site option "See other members of this site".
So turning on site (community) user visibility is what lets customers see one another — and therefore each other's Chatter posts — beyond their own account. Both settings apply only when the org-wide external default for the User object is Private; if it is Public Read Only, all users already see each other regardless.
There is no "View All for Chatter posts" setting, Chatter Super User is not the mechanism, and internal-user visibility governs a different direction of the relationship.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.networks_user_sharing.htm&language=en_US&type=5

optionC: Custom permissions
optionD: Profiles

Login hours that restrict when users can access Salesforce are configured on the Profile, so each call center's profile limits access to its local shift. Login hours are not set directly on the user record (A) or through permission sets or custom permissions (B and C).

question: Universal Containers (UC) has 200 distributors that use Partner Community licenses. Partners cannot see each other's data, but UC is also trying to give more visibility to data for certain individuals at a distributor. HOW can an Architect give users in the partner user role access to all Case and Container records owned by any user, regardless of role, at the same distributor?
optionA: Create an ownership-based sharing rule.
optionB: Create sharing sets.
optionC: Create a Permission Set granting "View All" permission to Case and Container records.
optionD: Give super user permission to the individual partner users.
explanation:
Granting Super User permission to a partner user gives access to all Case and Container records owned by users at their role and below at the same distributor, which is the scalable per-individual approach. Ownership-based rules (A) or sharing sets (B) do not cleanly target all users at one distributor, and a View All permission set (C) over-grants across distributors. Note that the phrase "any user regardless of role" strains super-user semantics, which grant access only to the same role and below.

question: Universal Containers has created a custom Sales Operations profile with read and edit access to the Category field on a custom object. There is a new requirement that 3 of the 100 users assigned to the Sales Operations Profile should have read-only access to the Category field. How can the Architect support this request? Choose one answer:
optionA: Create a permission set in the Category field to read-only and assign it to the users.
optionB: Create a new profile without edit access to Category and assign it to the users.
optionC: Create a new page layout with the Category Field set to read-only for these users.
optionD: Create a custom permission to grant read-only access to Category and assign it to the users.
explanation:
Field-Level Security through permission sets is additive, meaning it can only add access as a union and cannot remove the profile's existing edit access, so the only way to give three users read-only is a new profile without edit on the Category field. A read-only permission set (A, the source answer) cannot subtract edit, a read-only page layout (C) does not enforce FLS, and custom permissions (D) do not control FLS.

The architect at UC decided to surface the customer invoices in salesforce using external objects and did the following: -Configured an external object called Invoice. -Created a lookup relationship between account and the invoice. How can the architect grant the sales managers access to the customer invoices data?
optionA: By creating sharing rules to share the invoices records with users in sales mangers roles.
optionB: By creating manual sharing to share invoices with relevant sales managers.
optionC: By creating controlling the invoices object permission on the sales manager's profile.
optionD: By creating a sharing set to share invoices with users in sales manager role.
explanation:
For an external object with a lookup to Account, access is granted through the object-level permission on the profile, because sharing rules, sharing sets, and manual sharing do not apply to external objects. That is why A, B, and D are not valid for granting external-object access.

question: (Variant) Sales Operations at Universal Containers (UC) wants to create list views to filter opportunities for certain geographies. In which two ways can UC hide list views that are not relevant to an individual user since there will be many list views? Choose 2 answers.
optionA: Share the list views with the appropriate queue.
optionB: Share the list views with the appropriate individual users.
optionC: Share the list views with the appropriate public group.
optionD: Share the list views with the appropriate role in the role hierarchy
explanation:
List views are shown or hidden by their sharing target, and Salesforce describes the available choices as "All Users, Only Me, or Groups of Users" — where groups of users covers public groups and roles, including roles and subordinates. Pointing each geography's view at the matching group or role keeps a user's list-view picker down to what is relevant to them.
Individual users are not a target: "sharing a List View with a specific individual user is not natively supported", and the documented workaround is to wrap that user in a public group — which is option C by another route. Queues are not a list-view sharing target either.

https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.user_groups.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: At Universal Containers, Accounts and Contacts are normally visible to all employees, and Proposals (custom object) are visible to the Account owner and managers. However, some Proposals are considered confidential and are managed by a Strategic Proposals team. These Proposals should not be visible to anyone in the Sales group other than the owner and the strategic team. How should the architect design for this requirement?
optionA: Proposal Owner set to the Strategic Deals Team Queue and set the Account relationship to Master-Detail.
optionB: Disable Grant Access Using Hierarchies and set an Owner-Based Sharing rule for Strategic Deals team.
optionC: Proposal Owner set to the Strategic Deals Team Queue and create an owner-based sharing rule to grant visibility to the Account owner
optionD: Disable Grant Access Using Hierarchies and set a Criteria-Based Sharing rule for Strategic Deals team.
explanation:
Confidential proposals must be hidden from the wider Sales group, including managers above the owner, so disable "Grant Access Using Hierarchies" on Proposals to stop the hierarchy roll-up, then use an owner-based sharing rule to grant the Strategic Proposals team access. A criteria-based rule (D) would require a flag field and is less direct, and queue-owner approaches (A and C) do not isolate the records from the hierarchy. Note that disabling the hierarchy globally is in tension with normal proposals remaining visible to managers.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.security_controlling_access_using_hierarchies.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.security_sharing_rules_owner.htm&type=5&language=en_US

question: Universal Containers wants to create a way to store sensitive Invoice Data in Salesforce. A User who owns an Account should not see every Invoice, but only invoices that they or their subordinates own. Which two features should be considered during this solution implementation? Choose 2 answers.
optionA: Deploy the Relationship between Accounts and the Invoices Object as Master-Detail.
optionB: Ensure that the Organization-Wide Default sharing for Invoices is set to Private.
optionC: Create a Workflow that populates the Invoice sharing object upon Insert.
optionD: Deploy the Relationship between Accounts and the Invoices Object as Lookup.
explanation:
Owner-or-subordinates visibility requires the Role Hierarchy on a Private object, so the Invoice OWD must be Private (B) and the Account-to-Invoice relationship must be a Lookup (D) so invoices have their own owner and sharing. A Master-Detail relationship (A) would force Controlled-by-Parent and could not be Private, contradicting the requirement, which is why the source pairing of A and B is internally inconsistent.

question: Universal Containers has the following Sharing Settings for their Org: Account = Private Contact = Controlled by Parent Opportunity = Private Case = Private They have enabled "Default Account Teams" and have trained users to set up their Default Team. Which three access levels can be set on the Account Team Member? Choose 3 answers
optionA: Opportunity Access
optionB: Case Access
optionC: Contact Access
optionD: Contract Access
explanation:
Account Team member access can be set for the Account itself (E) and for child objects whose OWD is below Public Read/Write, here Opportunity (A) and Case (B), both Private. Contact is Controlled by Parent so it has no separate access setting, and there is no Contract Access option on account teams.

question: Partner users can access records belonging to users in their account at their same role or lower in the role hierarchy, for Cases, Leads, Opportunities and Custom Objects. Which of the following access has to be given?
optionA: Delegated External User Administrator
optionB: A sharing set granting access through the account
optionC: View All permission on each object
optionD: Partner Super User permission
explanation:
The Partner Super User permission (D) is what lets a partner user reach Cases, Leads, Opportunities, and custom object records owned by other users in their own account at the same role or below in the hierarchy. Delegated External User Administrator (A) grants the ability to manage other external users, not to see their records. Sharing sets (B) apply to Customer Community licences that have no role hierarchy, which is precisely the mechanism this question is not describing. View All (C) would expose every record of the object org-wide, far beyond the account-scoped access required.

question: Universal Containers has recently implemented an integration that is populating 50 custom fields on the account object. They would like these fields to be available to Managers for reporting but do not want them to clutter the page layouts. What should the Architect recommend as a solution?
optionA: Add the fields to the Managers' Account Page Layout; mark the page layout section as Collapsed.
optionB: Grant the Managers access to the fields using a Role-Based Sharing Rule; leave them hidden on the page layout.
optionC: Add the fields to a Custom Report; grant the Managers' Role access to the report folder.
optionD: Grant Managers access to the fields using Field-Level Security; do not add them to a page layout.
explanation:
Managers need the 50 fields for reporting but not on layouts, so grant access through Field-Level Security and simply leave the fields off the page layouts, because reporting reads FLS rather than layouts. Collapsed layout sections (A) still clutter, a sharing rule (B) does not control field visibility, and building a report (C) does not grant the underlying FLS.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.users_profiles_field_perms.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: The Corporate Identity and Access Team needs to audit User setup in the Salesforce .. What two permissions should be granted to this team so they can perform their audit? Choose 2 answers
optionA: View permission on the User object
optionB: View Setup and Configuration
optionC: View All Users
optionD: View All Data
explanation:
Auditing user setup requires "View Setup and Configuration" to inspect setup (B) and "View All Users" to see every user record (C). View on the User object (A) is narrower and not the audit permission, and View All Data (D) over-grants beyond the scope of a user-setup audit.

question: Assuming Person Account is enabled in a Salesforce organization, which three objects can be configured as "Controlled by Parent" in Sharing Settings? Choose 3 answers
optionA: Opportunity
optionB: Order
optionC: Asset
optionD: Contact
explanation:
